findings.evidence: by selecting an available time slot
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the required system behavior after a successful selection (e.g., 'The system shall confirm the booking and display a confirmation message').

Define the overlap condition precisely (e.g., 'overlaps if the start time of the new appointment is before the end time of the existing appointment AND the end time of the new appointment is after the start time of the existing appointment').

findings.evidence: Patients shall be able to cancel an appointment
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the mechanism or interface through which the patient can cancel the appointment (e.g., 'Patients shall be able to cancel an appointment via the patient portal').
Define a specific maximum response time (e.g., 'within 2 seconds').

Replace subjective terms with measurable criteria. For example, define 'seamless' by specifying maximum transition times between steps, or define 'delightful' by referencing a specific usability score (e.g., SUS score > 80).
Specify the exact retention period (e.g., 'for 7 years' or 'in accordance with regulatory standard XYZ').
Replace 'always' with specific uptime requirements (e.g., 'The system shall maintain 99.9% uptime during business hours').
Specify a concrete number or range for the number of concurrent users (e.g., 'The system shall support at least 100 concurrent users').

findings.evidence: The system shall send the visit invoice to the patient's insurer.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the trigger for sending the invoice (e.g., 'The system shall send the visit invoice to the patient's insurer immediately after the appointment is confirmed.')
Define a specific size threshold (e.g., 'when the log file size exceeds 100MB').
Specify the exact format (e.g., 'CSV format compliant with ISO 8601').

Define what 'robust' means in this context. For example, specify that the system shall return a specific error code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) and display a user-friendly message when invalid input is provided.
Define a specific time frame for sending the confirmation email (e.g., 'within 5 minutes of the appointment being confirmed').

Define the criteria for approval (e.g., 'shall be approved if the waiver request is submitted by a clinician and meets criteria X, Y, and Z') or define the expected outcome (e.g., 'shall be approved within 2 business days').
Define the starting point for determining the 'next' slots (e.g., 'The system shall display the clinician's next three available time slots starting from the current time').
Define 'easy to review' with measurable criteria, such as 'The log shall be reviewable within 5 seconds by an authorized user' or 'The log shall include fields X, Y, and Z for easy review.'
Specify the exact number of failed login attempts that will trigger the account lock (e.g., 'after 5 failed login attempts').
Specify the mechanism or interface through which appointment durations are configured (e.g., 'The system shall allow an administrator to configure appointment durations via the Admin Portal').
Define what 'override a booking' means (e.g., 'override a booking by changing its status to X' or 'override a booking by rescheduling it to Y').
Define the specific steps, rules, and actors involved in the 'pharmacy workflow' that prescription refills must follow.
Define what constitutes a 'major schedule change' (e.g., cancellation, rescheduling by more than 24 hours, etc.).
Define 'intuitive' by providing specific usability criteria or success metrics (e.g., 'The patient portal shall allow a first-time user to complete the booking process in under 3 steps').
Specify a measurable time threshold for loading (e.g., 'The patient portal shall load within 3 seconds under normal network conditions').

findings.evidence: when a patient cancels an appointment
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the maximum allowable time between the cancellation event and the clinician receiving the notification (e.g., 'within 5 minutes').
